answer: Each identity runs one knoll post above a dune crest, bonded at 70 credits. At zenith each epoch it files a key-signed skyline reading of its dune view angles plus its serial. The auditor recomputes the silhouette from the dune survey; over 2 degrees off, a reused serial, or a missing filing burns the bond. The first filing costs 34; the k-th post costs 34+7(k-1), so the 1000th costs 7027 and 1000 fakes pay 3,530,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-skyline ring fails: copied readings carry a wrong or duplicate serial, burning both bonds. Honest posts pay 34 once, bond back after a clean epoch.
